description: Tracked inventory of every known status edge case. Each entry names its reproducing fixture in this directory, the guard that closes it (a test `tests/<file>::<name>` or a module symbol `<module>::<symbol>`), and a one-line root cause. tests/test_detection_replay.py::test_edge_case_inventory_is_closed_and_consistent fails CI when a fixture or guard disappears, and when a fixture tagged edge_case is not registered here.

late_hook_reopen.root_cause: Hooks are an unordered retried side channel; a late PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit can land after the transcript's end-of-turn and reopen working on a finished session.

closed_by_transcript_latch.root_cause: Defense-in-depth behind the authority gate: once the transcript closes a turn, a hook-sourced re-begin is refused (and counted) until fresh transcript activity starts the next turn.

hook_transcript_race_trailing_completion.root_cause: The reverse race: a trailing assistant end_turn record landing after a hook Stop already closed the turn used to re-begin and immediately re-finish, blinking the status working for an instant.

ended_stuck_force_idle.root_cause: A lost Stop hook (failed POST, spool not yet drained) leaves working forever even though the transcript tail proves the turn ended; the watchdog force-idles at STATE_WATCHDOG_ENDED_STUCK_SECONDS.

esc_pause_without_marker.root_cause: ESC can pause a turn without writing the interrupt marker, leaving an open tool tail with no terminal record; only the PTY idle-prompt backstop may recover it after STATE_WATCHDOG_PTY_STUCK_SECONDS.

long_tool_esc_interrupt.root_cause: A genuine long tool call reads as an open tail too; 'esc to interrupt' on screen keeps pty_tail_appears_idle False so the backstop never cuts it short.

sibling_transcript_cross_attribution.root_cause: With sibling sessions in one cwd a fresh sibling transcript is indistinguishable from an in-CLI resume; following it would bleed the sibling's status into this record. The switch is gated, and the PTY backstop (own ground truth) recovers the stuck session.

schema_drift_unknown_tail.root_cause: Schema drift can leave the tail with no decisive signal (unknown); the conservative prior keeps the session working until the PTY idle-prompt backstop proves the CLI is at its prompt.

crash_mid_turn.root_cause: A process death mid-turn produces no transcript terminal record; PTY ground truth maps the exit code to crashed/exited and permanently blocks delivery.

compaction_mid_turn.root_cause: Compaction boundaries are telemetry, not turn evidence; treating them as activity would reopen or close turns spuriously.

resume_open_turn_recent.root_cause: Promotion moments after the user submitted attaches over an open turn; a recent open tail must resume as working, not idle.

resume_open_turn_stale.root_cause: An old open turn found during catch-up is a stale artifact of an ended run; resuming it as working would strand the session.

approval_answered_resume.root_cause: An approval is raised by an unordered hook (priority 2) while every resumption record arrives on the ordered transcript (priority 1), and `_begin_root_turn` deliberately does not release arbitration while the state is working/awaiting — so arbitration refused all of it and the session displayed "awaiting approval" for the entire rest of the turn (observed live: 558s across two further approvals). Transcript evidence written after the block now clears it.

approval_answered_long_tool.root_cause: Nothing fires when a permission dialog is dismissed, and an approved long-running tool writes no transcript record until it completes, so no ordered evidence exists to clear the block; the CLI's own working spinner is the only timely proof.

pending_approval_preserved.root_cause: The inverse hazard of clearing a stale awaiting: the tool_use record that triggered the prompt can be observed after it, a parallel tool's result can land while the dialog is up, and idle_prompt can arrive — none of which mean the user answered. Hiding a real prompt is worse than showing a stale one, so clearing requires proof (record newer than the block, screen not showing a dialog).

notification_semantics.root_cause: idle_prompt means ready-for-input (a turn boundary), not a blocking approval; permission_prompt and elicitation_dialog are awaiting with distinct sub-reasons, and idle_prompt must never overwrite a pending approval.

subagent_stop_root_open.root_cause: Child stops are subagent-scoped activity; letting them complete the root turn shows idle while the root is still working.

rate_limit_abort.root_cause: A provider rate limit is awaiting (sub-reason rate_limit), and the subsequent aborted turn must resolve to idle on transcript evidence, never linger as working.

daemon_restart_mid_turn.root_cause: A daemon restart mid-turn loses volatile completion evidence; readiness must re-require a fresh root lifecycle boundary instead of trusting pre-restart state.

promotion_demotion_status.root_cause: Promotion/demotion are daemon-owned lifecycle transitions (starting/running); they must flow through the ledger and reset source arbitration for the new backend's evidence.

unwitnessed_first_turn_pty_only.root_cause: Codex has no session-start hook and mints its own thread id, which it names only on agent-turn-complete, so for the whole first turn a fresh pane has neither a bound transcript nor a hook. `working` was reachable from neither source, so the startup-quiet PTY fallback's `idle` was the last word and the pane read 'ready - turn complete' while the agent worked (measured live at 200 s).

provisional_transcript_attribution.root_cause: Following the sole unclaimed rollout by elimination lets the first turn be observed, but the file is a guess: rekeying native_session_id from it, writing the history row, or publishing its tokens would render a stranger's conversation under this pane's identity.

nested_child_hook_cross_attribution.root_cause: The hook ingress and secret authenticate the session, not the process: a nested claude launched by this session's own tool call inherits the wiring and speaks over the same channel. Its SessionStart(startup) rolled the parent's identity onto the child's conversation (14 times, live 2026-07-31) and its PermissionRequest pinned 'awaiting approval' for a dialog on no visible screen. Rollovers now require an in-place replacement (clear/resume, same cwd) and a bound session's state only listens to its own conversation; the pane's spawn conversation speaking while bound elsewhere heals the identity back.

modern_cli_marker_drift.root_cause: Claude Code 2.x removed 'esc to interrupt' and '? for shortcuts' and draws dialog phrases one column-positioned word at a time, so the raw-substring markers matched nothing and every screen-based recovery (resume_working above all) silently disabled — sessions displayed 'awaiting approval' through minutes of visible work. Markers now target the frame-recurring spinner ellipsis and the current dialog/footer affordances, matched over cursor-normalized text, with real captured streams pinned as fixtures.

standing_annotation_never_latches.root_cause: A standing-activity annotation whose clearing evidence never arrives (killed loop runner, lost completion record) would otherwise display forever — the annotation-axis version of every stuck-status incident. Every annotation the evidence bounds carries an expiry, the watchdog's TTL sweep decays it, and each decay counts in status health as standing_activity_expired.

foreign_subagent_hook_annotation.root_cause: A nested child CLI inherits the hook wiring, so its SubagentStart/SubagentStop arrive on the parent's ingress naming the child's conversation; counting them would render the child's fleet as this session's subagents. The foreign-conversation filter runs before annotation extraction, so a foreign lifecycle hook is ledgered and dropped without touching the annotation set.

startup_dialog_reads_idle.root_cause: Claude's workspace-trust dialog appears after its SessionStart hook already reported idle, and Codex's trust/update dialogs appear before any evidence channel exists — so a blocked session displayed 'ready' while typed input landed in the dialog (measured live in E2E). The watchdog now raises awaiting(approval) from a sustained approval screen, but only on a session no turn has ever run, and only that rule may clear it when the screen moves on.

startup_dialog_reads_idle_codex.root_cause: The Codex variant of the startup-dialog gap: no session-start hook and no transcript exist before turn one, so the startup-quiet idle was the last word while a trust/update dialog blocked the pane. Same rule, same guard — the unwitnessed pair deliberately cannot act on an approval screen, so only the startup-dialog rule can represent it.

background_completion_queued_not_message.root_cause: A background shell that finishes while its session is between turns has no turn to be announced into, so the CLI queues the notification: it lands as a `queue-operation` record and its `attachment` mirror, and only becomes a user message if the CLI later hands it to the model. The extractors read only the user form, so the annotation stayed open for its full 30-minute TTL while the proof of completion sat in the transcript the whole time (measured live 2026-08-06 on a session showing a hollow blue ring with every one of its background shells long dead). All three carriers now close, idempotently per task, because duplicate announcements are the normal case.

background_pty_footer_reopen.root_cause: The CLI's background-wait footer is corroboration, but `set_standing_activity` creates when absent, which quietly made it a source. Read over a 32 KiB append-only window of redraw traffic, the footer drawn while a task genuinely ran stays matchable long after it finished: measured live 2026-08-06, the transcript positively closed the annotation and this reading re-added it 29 s later with a fresh 30-minute TTL, after which nothing but that TTL could clear it. The tier is now refresh-only, the same rule the subagent tier's `create=False` already had, and its markers must name a count so arbitrary prose on screen cannot satisfy them.

screen_classifier_blind_alarm.root_cause: The 2026-07-31 marker-drift incident ran for weeks with pty_tail_state returning unknown on every busy screen — every screen-based recovery silently disabled, discovered only by a user report. A witnessed session continuously working for the blind window while every read returns unknown now counts screen_classifier_blind (once per window, never changing state), and two blind sessions raise the fleet status-health alarm.
